title: The Mechanics of (Poro-)Elastic Contractile Actomyosin Networks As a Model System of the Cell Cytoskeleton
protocol: Use Piranha solution for glass surface cleaning.
Incubate the polytetrafluoroethylene holder with 300 mL of Piranha solution for 2 hours on ice in a chemical hood.
Pour the used Piranha solution into water to achieve a 50x dilution before discarding.
Transfer the polytetrafluoroethylene holder into a clean beaker filled with fresh double-distilled water.
Sonicate the beaker in a sonication bath at 80 Hz for 10 minutes at 25 °C.
Repeat the washing and sonication steps two more times with fresh double-distilled water each time.
Transfer the holder into a clean beaker containing 300 mL of pure methanol.
Sonicate the holder in the methanol solution at 80 Hz for 30 minutes at 25 °C.
Prepare a silane solution using 15 mL of DDW, 3.1 mL of acetic acid, 340 mL of methanol, and 7.6 mL of (3-Mercaptopropyl) trimethoxysilane.
Seal the beaker containing the silane solution with parafilm and store it in a refrigerator at 4 °C overnight.
Transfer the holder into a clean beaker filled with 300 mL of pure methanol for 15 seconds on the following day.
Dry the bottom of the polytetrafluoroethylene holder to remove excess methanol.
Place the holder in an oven and dry it for 5 minutes at 120 °C.
Achieve surface passivation by incubating the glass coverslips with an inert polymer.
Take two coverslips and place them in a Petri dish coated with a parafilm layer initially cleaned with ethanol (EtOH).
Incubate each coverslip with 1 mL of a 4 mg·mL−1 5 kDa molecular weight methoxy polyethylene glycol maleimide (mPEG-mal, Mw = 5 kDa) in 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for 1 h at 22 °C.
Rinse each coverslips with 5 mL of distilled deionized water (DDW).
Dry the coverslips with a flow of nitrogen gas (N2).
Place 1 mL of 10 mM Tris on the pegylated surfaces immediately after drying.
Keep the coverslips wet after passivation and use them within 2 h.
Keep purified G-actin in G-buffer and store on ice.
Replace the ice every couple of days for actin storage.
Label the actin with a maleimide-modified fluorescent dye.
Purify GST-fascin based on the method described by Ono et al.
Flash-freeze both proteins in liquid N2 and store at -80°C.
Purify myosin II from rabbit skeletal muscle using a standard protocol.
Store purified myosin II in stock buffer including 10 mM Tris pH 7.4, 0.5 M KCl, and 35% w/v sucrose.
Flash-freeze the purified myosin II in liquid N2 and store at -80°C.
Label the myosin II dimers with a fluorescent dye at pairs of engineered cysteine residues.
Use chicken gizzard RLC mutant A for labeling myosin II.
Flash-freeze the labeled myosin II in liquid N2 and store at -80°C.
Use a UV-Vis spectrophotometer to measure the absorbance of stock protein solutions.
Deduce protein concentrations using the Beer-Lambert law with given extinction coefficients for G-actin, GST-fascin, myosin II dimer, and RLC mutant A.
Thaw proteins at 37°C before use, except for G-actin.
Prepare actomyosin solution by mixing specified components in a total volume of 40 µL.
Include 10 mM Tris pH 7.4, 2 mM MgCl2, 25 mM KCl, 1 mM ATP, an ATP regenerating system, 200 µM EGTA, an anti-bleaching solution, 5 µM G-actin, 280 nM GST-fascin, and 1.67 nM myosin II.
Use a low percentage of labeled G-actin to avoid signal saturation during gel contraction.
Dilute the myosin stock solution with 10 mM Tris pH 7.4 to reach a final concentration of 25 mM KCl.
Incubate the diluted myosin solution for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the myosin solution to ice and keep it until use.
Add fluorescent beads to the actomyosin solution to track solvent flow across gel pores.
Incubate 1 µL of beads with 5 µM G-actin for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge the mixture (6,000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C) to remove excess G-actin.
Repeat incubation with 10 mg·mL−1 bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Centrifuge again after BSA treatment to block remaining uncoated surface of beads.
Use the beads at a final dilution of 1:10,000 vol/vol in experiments.
Add glycerol to the actomyosin solution to control viscosity.
Increase glycerol concentration from 0% to 34% to increase solution viscosity from ηω to 2.76 ηω.
Take one PEG-passivated coverslip.
Place a greased parafilm spacer on top of the coverslip.
Place the covered coverslip in the sample holder.
Prepare the actomyosin solution on ice by incorporating microscopic constituents, myosin II motor aggregates, and adding EGTA last.
Mix the actomyosin solution well after adding EGTA.
Put 1.1 µL of the prepared solution onto the holder-mounted coverslip.
Place a second coverslip on top to seal the sample.
Screw the holder to secure the sealed sample.
Place the sample holder on the microscope.
Start the acquisition immediately after placing the sample holder on the microscope.
Image the samples using an inverted fluorescent microscope.
Use a 2.5x/0.075 Plan-NEOFLUAR objective to visualize the whole gel area.
Characterize the network porosity and structure with a 10x/0.3 Ph1 UPlanFL objective.
Locate myosin II motor aggregates within the network using the 10x objective.
Follow the movement of fluorescent beads across the gel pores.
Excite samples at 488 nm for actin and fluorescent beads.
Excite samples at 561 nm for myosin motor aggregates and fluorescent beads.
Acquire images at 100 ms per frame with dedicated software.
Use an electron multiplying charge-coupled device (EMCCD) camera for imaging.
Keep the fluorescent lamp intensity at the lowest possible value to avoid signal saturation.
Excite the actin network at 488 nm and myosin II motors at 561 nm simultaneously.
Record images of the actin gel and fluorescent beads using an EMCCD camera.
Simultaneously image the actin gel at 488 nm and the fluorescent beads at 561 nm.
